definition: Winner-take-all is a computational principle applied in computational models of neural networks by which neurons compete with each other for activation.
details: In the classical form, only the neuron with the highest activation stays active while all other neurons shut down; however, other variations allow more than one neuron to be active, for example the soft winner take-all, by which a power function is applied to the neurons.

explainer.lead: Winner-take-all is a computational principle in neural network models where neurons compete for activation. It matters because it enforces sparse, competitive selection of the most active unit.

tiers.eli5: It's like a race where only the fastest runner gets the prize and everyone else stops; some versions let a few runners share the prize.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to let only the strongest activation drive the output, or variants like soft winner-take-all that keep several units active. A pitfall is that strict winner-take-all discards all but one neuron's signal.
tiers.paperLevel: In the classical form, only the neuron with the highest activation stays active while all others shut down; soft winner-take-all applies a power function to the neurons so more than one can remain active.

explainer.example: In a layer of competing units, the unit with the highest activation remains on and the rest are set to zero; a soft variant raises activations to a power so a few units stay partly active.
